Version 0.2.0 adds **offline exact search** alongside GPU board repair. Choose pruned DFS, Glucose SAT, or OR-Tools CP-SAT in the dashboard. DFS uses color/rotation domains, adjacency propagation, piece uniqueness, and perfect-matching feasibility checks; its remaining search is checkpointed on Stop and resumed on Start. SAT and CP-SAT restart their native search on each start.

The bounded local comparison did not find a full 480/480 solution or establish a fastest full-puzzle algorithm. Pruned DFS is the fallback recommendation, with SAT and CP-SAT available for comparison. The portable DFS implementation is Python; its timings are not a benchmark of optimized native backtrackers. See docs/EXACT_SEARCH.md for tested scope and limits.

An experimental hybrid option first samples complete random legal boards on the GPU, including low-scoring arrangements, then freezes at most64 validated candidates to guide CPU DFS ordering. Hints never eliminate valid search branches. Its measured whole-board sampling rate is separate from CPU screening, uniqueness and solution progress; no solving speedup is established. Hybrid hints and checkpoints stay separate from plain DFS and GPU repair.

Exact engines use the CPU and target all 480 edges with all five official clues. They retain the saved best board until an independently validated complete solution is found. Their branches/conflicts are local diagnostic counters, not production BOINC tickets, nodes, or credit. The existing GPU repair engines remain available through CUDA and OpenCL.

All normal operation remains offline: no automatic library refreshes, telemetry, or result uploads. **Export best board** writes independently validated files locally for manual review. The project submission schema remains unconfirmed. Opening the app starts only its local dashboard; search requires Start. Existing GPU checkpoints remain separate from the DFS checkpoint.

Native packages cover Windows x64, Linux x64, macOS Intel, and macOS Apple Silicon. Windows/Linux include CUDA and OpenCL; macOS uses OpenCL. Compatible hardware drivers are needed for GPU search. Every native package runs frozen exact-engine SAT/UNSAT diagnostics and resource/export checks. Linux additionally checks source and frozen OpenCL on PoCL's CPU device; these checks do not certify physical AMD, Intel, or Apple GPUs. macOS packages are not Apple-notarized.

No user checkpoints, downloaded library databases, local discoveries, logs, or credentials are packaged. Dependency versions, licenses and resource checksums accompany each archive. The BOINC CPU inspector and wrapper examples remain research tools, not approved production applications; the standalone exact mode does not reproduce or submit BOINC workunits.
